Watch status transitions: `submitted` → `working` → `completed` L82: ## JWT Authentication L83: L84: Enable JWT authentication by setting the `JWT_SECRET` environment variable: L85: L86: ```bash L87: JWT_SECRET=my-secret PYTHONPATH=./examples/binding_demo python examples/run.py L88: ``` L89: L90: ### Test Token L91: L92: Pre-generated token (secret: `my-secret`, algorithm: HS256): L93: L94: ``` L95: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJkZW1vLXVzZXIiLCJ0eXBlIjoidXNlciIsInJvbGVzIjpbImFkbWluIl19.yOFQMlZnMZwXg6KoJX61sCm2VbCzmqtT8dFRNsOhaZM L96: ``` L97: L98: Payload: L99: L100: ```json L101: {"sub": "demo-user", "type": "user", "roles": ["admin"]} L102: ``` L103: ### Verify with cURL L104: L105: ```bash L106: TOKEN="eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJkZW1vLXVzZXIiLCJ0eXBlIjoidXNlciIsInJvbGVzIjpbImFkbWluIl19.yOFQMlZnMZwXg6KoJX61sCm2VbCzmqtT8dFRNsOhaZM" L107: L108: # Agent card (always accessible; 0.3 alias /.well-known/agent.json also served) L109: curl http://localhost:8000/.well-known/agent-card.json L110: # Send message without auth L111: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/ \ L112: -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ L113: -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"msg-1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"Hello!"}]}}}' L114: # Send message with auth L115: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/ \ L116: -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ L117: -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ L118: -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"msg-1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"Hello!"}]}}}' L119: ``` L120: ### Explorer UI with JWT L121: L122: The Explorer UI at http://127.0.0.1:8000/explorer/ is always accessible without authentication. The agent card and skill browser work without a token. Message sending and streaming will include the auth token stored in `sessionStorage` if available. L123: L124: ## Comparing with apcore-mcp L125: L126: The same apcore modules work with both protocols: L127: L128: ```bash L129: # Serve as A2A agent L130: apcore-a2a serve --extensions-dir ./examples/extensions --explorer L131: # Serve as MCP server (using apcore-mcp) L132: apcore-mcp serve --extensions-dir ./examples/extensions --transport streamable-http --explorer --allow-execute L133: ``` L134: L135: Same modules, same Registry, different protocols.
